clue.text: Might describe the school outlook to us

parts.note: an outlook or view ahead is a prospect
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether the school's future looks good for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link joining the two pieces. The definition is loose: a school's brochure describing it to parents.
explanation.definitionFit: A school publishes a brochure setting out its courses and facilities for prospective parents.

clue.text: Sapper groups hold it up — stop work,

indicators.note: hold means the two engineer units contain the other piece between them

parts.note: sappers are the Royal Engineers, RE; two such groups give RE twice

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word it is read bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Army engineers stall a job, and work comes to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the little word upwards, as fits a down entry, and 'hold' has the doubled engineers' letters close round it. Sappers are soldiers of the Royal Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up one's working life, as on reaching pensionable age.

clue.text: Might be the summer one found close — its unusual

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of close and its come in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A summer day is unusually close and humid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges CLOSEITS. 'close' looks like the weather, but is just fodder; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest day of the year is the summer one, an astronomical turning point.

clue.text: Going to settle share taken by East Russian fighter

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter plane
a ration is one's allotted share

explanation.surface: A Russian soldier takes his portion as he moves east to make a home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' puts the share after E and MIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving one's country to live permanently abroad.

clue.text: Number of scholars found in a body

parts.note: ten is a number
dons are university teachers and scholars

explanation.surface: How many academics belong to some learned society?
explanation.walkthrough: 'body' suggests an academic body; it is the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough cords of tissue joining muscle to bone are part of human anatomy.

clue.text: A fuel rise — it's the old tale!

indicators.note: in a down clue, a rise reads a fuel from the bottom upwards

parts.note: gas is a fuel

explanation.surface: Complaining that fuel prices are up again: the same old story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' reverses AGAS. It looks like a price increase.
explanation.definitionFit: A long Norse or Icelandic prose story of heroes is an old narrative.

clue.text: Plot revolution on prices

indicators.note: revolution turns the letters of on and prices around into a new order

explanation.surface: Rebels scheme an uprising over the cost of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' rearranges ONPRICES; it looks like a political uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To scheme together secretly, as in planning a coup.

clue.text: Using no deputy, unisex type overcomes comrade in arms

indicators.note: in a down clue, overcomes puts the first piece over, above, the second

parts.note: person is a word of no gender, a unisex term
an ally fights alongside you

explanation.surface: A gender-neutral figure beats a fellow soldier without a stand-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overcomes' looks like defeat, but in a down entry it means sits above.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something oneself rather than through an agent.

clue.text: Jack gets in some port — that's going it!

definitions.text: Jack gets in some port — that's going it!

parts.words: Jack gets in some port — that's going it
parts.note: Jack is a sailor; when he steps off the ship into a harbour town he is going onto dry land

explanation.surface: A sailor arrives at a harbour and heads off for a spree.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack (Jack Tar) is crossword shorthand for a sailor; 'going it' suggests living it up, but the phrase completes 'going ...' for a sailor leaving the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor landing at a port leaves the vessel for dry land, the beach side of the quay.

clue.text: Seat one on a horse

parts.note: a stall is a seat in a theatre or a church choir
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to put someone up in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat' reads as a verb, but it is the noun: a theatre stall. 'a' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse kept for breeding is a stud animal of that name.

clue.text: Their records appear dated, no doubt

definitions.text: Their records appear dated, no doubt

parts.words: Their records appear dated, no doubt
parts.note: 'dated' seems to mean old-fashioned, but journal keepers head every entry with the day it was written

explanation.surface: Somebody's old files look out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dated' suggests out of fashion; the cryptic sense is that every entry carries a date.
explanation.definitionFit: People who keep a daily journal write entries each headed with the date.

clue.text: The mythical creature in Hyperion

indicators.note: the creature's name sits inside the word Hyperion, between its first two and last two letters

explanation.surface: Asking which fabulous being appears in Keats's poem Hyperion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside the name Hyperion (a Titan, and a Keats poem).
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth a peri is a fairy or beautiful spirit, a fabulous being.

clue.text: Literary giant has sort of an apt punishment

indicators.note: sort of signals the letters of an apt are sorted into a new order

parts.note: gruel is punishment, as in 'take one's gruel'

explanation.surface: A great writer gets a fitting comeuppance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges ANAPT into PANTA. 'Literary giant' suggests a great author, but is a literal giant from Rabelais.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabelais's huge character, son of Gargantua, is a giant in literature.

clue.text: Denying backward scholar translated Antigone

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the letters for the scholar the other way round

parts.note: a BA (Bachelor of Arts) is a scholar

indicators.note: translated means the letters of the name Antigone are rendered into a new form

explanation.surface: A reluctant student puts Sophocles' Antigone into English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns BA into AB; 'translated' rearranges ANTIGONE into NEGATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-denial or renunciation is the sense: refusing oneself something.

clue.text: Rule can get broken by family man

indicators.note: broken means the letters of rule can get are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A regulation may be flouted by a father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges RULECANGET; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's uncle is a male relative two generations up.

clue.text: Jolly good quarters given to people returning to plant

indicators.note: returning means the whole run of jolly good, quarters and people is read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, jolly good; the 1 is read as the letter I
south and east are two quarters of the compass, SE
men are people

explanation.surface: Generous lodgings are handed over to workers coming back to the factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses AISEMEN to give the answer. 'plant' looks like a factory, but it is a garden flower; 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A South African flowering annual grown as a bedding flower in gardens.

clue.text: Letters from girls — about four

indicators.note: about means the girls go round the other piece

parts.note: misses are young girls
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: Correspondence from young women concerning a foursome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it means the young women's word goes round the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal written messages sent to someone.

clue.text: Roosevelt's reforms followed some cutting?

definitions.meaning: the programme of economic recovery measures brought in by Franklin D. Roosevelt in the 1930s
at cards, after the pack is cut, the cards are dealt out again

explanation.surface: A history question: did FDR's programme come after spending cuts?
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' suggests budget cuts; the second reading is cutting a pack of cards, after which a fresh hand is dealt.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1930s US recovery programme, and a fresh hand dealt after the cards are cut.

clue.text: Ruling given in note

definitions.meaning: in music, the fifth degree of a scale

explanation.surface: A judgment is handed down in a written memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given in' links the two definitions; 'note' is a musical note, not a written one.
explanation.definitionFit: Controlling or prevailing; and in music the fifth degree of the scale.

clue.text: One animal (or two?) in cabaret, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that cabaret might be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A creature, or maybe a pair, performing in a nightclub show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CABARET; 'in' is a link. '(or two?)' because the name joins a bear and a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A name for the binturong or red panda, a single beast whose name joins two others.

clue.text: Document shows task allotted

definitions.meaning: in law, a deed transferring property or rights to someone
a piece of work given out to someone to do

explanation.surface: A piece of paper sets out the work someone has been given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shows' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Legally, a deed transferring rights; generally, a job set for someone.

clue.text: Girl landed in the USA

parts.note: a girl's name with 'land' added becomes an American state, so the girl has been 'landed' in the USA

explanation.surface: A young woman arrives in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landed' seems to mean arrived; the trick is adding LAND to the name to give the state of Maryland.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name which, with land added, names an eastern US state.

clue.text: Old enough to enter navy and get fame

indicators.note: to enter means old enough goes inside the navy letters

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
enow is an archaic word for enough

explanation.surface: Someone is now old enough to join the navy and win glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old enough' seems to be about age, but means an old word for 'enough', ENOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity or wide acclaim.

clue.text: Animal associated with present transport

parts.note: 'present' seems to mean current-day, but means gifts: the beasts that pull Father Christmas's sleigh

explanation.surface: Asking which creature is linked with modern means of travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' reads as 'current', but it is a gift: the animals carry Santa's presents.
explanation.definitionFit: Antlered Arctic deer pull Santa's sleigh laden with Christmas gifts.

clue.text: Stop losing head and relax!

indicators.note: losing head means the word for stop drops its first letter

parts.note: to cease is to stop

explanation.surface: An exhortation to quit fretting and calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' removes the C of CEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen up or slacken off.

clue.text: Bird writing another article also

parts.note: another bird, the cock or rooster
a is the indefinite article
too means also

explanation.surface: A bird composes one more piece for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing another' means you write the bird as another bird, then an article, then 'also'. 'article' suggests a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article A.
explanation.definitionFit: A crested parrot of Australasia is a familiar example of this feathered type.

clue.text: Leaves direction to go with collection of taxes

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

indicators.note: a collection of the letters of taxes gathers them up in a different order

explanation.surface: A tax collector is told where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection of' rearranges TAXES into XEATS. 'Leaves' looks like a verb but is the plural noun: permissions to be away.
explanation.definitionFit: At British schools and colleges, a permit for a pupil to be absent is a leave of absence of this Latin name.

clue.text: Begging letter written before negotiation

parts.note: en is the name of the letter N in printing
treating with someone is negotiating with them

explanation.surface: A pleading letter is drafted before talks begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests a written appeal, but it is a printer's letter, EN; 'written before' places it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleading or imploring someone earnestly.
